news.title: Moroccan officials selected for Qatar U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Moroccan refereeing has made a new mark on the global stage after FIFA announced the official list of referees who will officiate matches at the U-17 World Cup, scheduled to take place in Qatar. The list includes the names of two Moroccan referees: Mohamed Al-Baroudi, as the head referee, and Abdel Samad Aberton, as part of the assistant referee team, ensuring that Moroccan refereeing is represented in one of the world’s most prominent youth competitions. FIFA has selected 81 referees and refereeing officials to participate in the tournament, which Qatar will host from November 19 to December 13, 2026. The selection of Al-Baroudi and Aberton reinforces the presence of Moroccan referees in international competitions and underscores FIFA’s continued reliance on Moroccan refereeing expertise on the global stage.

news.title: Infantino under pressure to include abandoned World Cup sell-off plan in external Fifa review
news.lede: Council members also want Balogun affair included. Fifa president says review letter been well received. Fifa council members will demand that Gianni Infantino include the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the Folarin Balogun affair in his proposed external review of Fifa’s governance. In a letter sent to all 211 of Fifa’s member associations on Monday, Infantino said he would ask the council to commission a review of “Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives” at its next meeting, in Zurich on 15 October, but he faces an internal battle over its terms of reference.

news.title: Jude Bellingham earns World Cup award he didn’t even know existed
news.lede: The England midfielder has admitted he did not know the award existed, though. Bellingham scored seven goals in eight appearances for the Three Lions in North America this summer. His goals included braces against both Mexico and Norway as well as a strike in the third place play-off against France. The 23-year-old ended the World Cup as the third-highest scorer behind Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi, who scored 10 and eight goals, respectively.

news.title: The stadium hosting the NFL's first Rio game has a rich history, including World Cup title games
news.lede: RIO DE JANEIRO (AP) — American football will make its debut in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday at a futebol cathedral. The 78,000-seat Maracana Stadium is a revered soccer venue that has hosted two World Cup championship games, Olympic gold medal matches for men and women, and numerous clashes between South America's biggest teams. Now the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys will play the NFL’s first game in Rio there, one of a record nine international contests on the league schedule this season. Built for the 1950 World Cup, the Mário Filho Stadium in the northern end of the city is universally known as the Maracana due to the river that flows behind it.

news.title: Ronaldo was ready to walk away from Portugal after World Cup, but one burning belief changed his mind ahe
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has admitted that he seriously considered ending his Portugal career after this summer’s World Cup, but the decision ultimately came down to whether he still believed he could contribute. Now 41 and approaching his 234th international appearance, Ronaldo has chosen to continue, with a new coach, a young generation around him and another Nations League campaign ahead. Cristiano Ronaldo, at 41, contemplates his future with the Portugal national team but chooses to continue following discussions with officials, citing his ability to contribute to the squad as the key factor in his decision.

news.title: Bonus for the World Cup: Spain star gives up one million euros to federation employees
news.lede: A press report revealed today, Thursday, a stunning surprise concerning one of the players of the Spain national team, crowned champions of the 2026 World Cup. Money isn't always everything in football, according to newspaper "AS", and it pointed to a fresh example: someone who will wear two stars on his chest this Saturday at Wembley Stadium, where Spain face England in the UEFA Nations League. The player in question, whose identity the paper did not reveal, gave up his World Cup winning bonus and donated it to the staff of the Spanish Football Federation in appreciation of their outstanding efforts. news.title: Virgil van Dijk says reports he decided Netherlands tactics at World Cup are ‘utter nonsense’
news.lede: Virgil van Dijk has hit back at criticism following the Netherlands’ World Cup failure and dismissed claims that he was responsible for the team changing tactics.The Netherlands defender insisted tactical decisions were made by the coaching staff and described suggestions that he and Ronald Koeman had “destroyed Dutch football” as “utter nonsense”.“.
